rationale: Evidence from the baseline (entityR2A, 60 trials, zero finishes): every trial went off track, with progress of only 0.04 to 0.125 and one line-loss event per run. Max error sat at about 0.06 m, the off-track limit, while steering_oscillation stayed low (about 0.07). The robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily away from the line, and the drift is similar on all three tracks, including the oval, which is the easiest. A steady drift like this points to a constant bias. The likely source is the fixed left/right motor mismatch in the simulator. With proportional-only control, a constant bias leaves a standing offset of roughly bias/kp in signal, so the robot never returns to centre and eventually leaves the tape, then loses the line. Geometry is kept unchanged so this race isolates the controller. The change is one group only: add integral action with ki = 0.6 to cancel the constant bias. The integral is clamped at ±2 by the contract, so it cannot wind up badly. kp stays at 5 and kd at 0.1, and base_speed stays at 1.4 because speed does not appear to be the cause. Expected result: rms_error falls well below 0.03 m, max_error stays clear of 0.06 m, and progress rises toward 1.0 on the oval. Hypotheses to test next: (1) if progress still stalls near the same point, the bias is larger than ki can handle, or the robot is losing the line at a specific bend, which would point to widening the outer sensors to x = ±0.06; (2) if the robot now oscillates, reduce kp to 4 and keep kd at 0.1; (3) if it finishes with a time above about 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation.
